# Ease Language Reference (1-Page LLM Guide)

Ease is a small, strict, bracket-free language implemented in Go.
Every construct has **one canonical form** and **zero silent fallbacks**.

## 1. Core Invariants
- **No `bool`, no `true`/`false` literals, no storable conditions**: Keep conditions (`x > 0`, `a is b`, `contains txt sub`, `and`, `or`, `not`) inside `check`, `where`, and `test` (there is no `if` keyword). Conditions cannot be stored, printed, passed, or returned (`ok = 3 > 2`, `ok = contains "a" "a"`, or `say 3 > 2` raises `TypeError: Conditions cannot be stored or printed...`). Return or store outcomes via explicit `def` union types/records (`def status = "OK" | "FAILED"`, `def decision` with `answer = "yes" | "no"`). All text boundaries (source, `ask`, `http_call`, `decode_json`) reject invalid UTF-8 and normalize to Unicode NFC.
- **Two `check` forms & arrow semantics (`->`)**: Use single-line `check <cond> -> <expr_or_stmt>` for flat guards/loop filters, and block `check ... end` for exhaustive union matches and `else` fallbacks (bare `check` without `->` or `else` is a parse error; abort explicitly with `check <cond> -> fail "..."`). Inside a `to` function, `-> <value>` returns immediately from the whole function (even out of `loop`), while `-> <stmt>` (`say`, assignment) executes and continues. Because `append` does not mutate in place and any unassigned expression after `->` inside `to` returns immediately, always write `check cond -> xs = append xs val`, never `check cond -> append xs val`. Inside `loop`, `check <cond> -> end` exits only the innermost `loop`. At top level, `check <cond> -> <value>` is an error (`Cannot return a value from 'check' at top level; use 'say' or 'fail' instead.`).
- **Pattern matching & structured extraction (`match ... end`)**: Matches full strings against `"..."` templates with `{...}` wildcards, `{name}` (`0+` runes, minimal left-to-right), `{name: N}` fixed rune widths (`N >= 1`), and `{name as number|<Union>}` typed captures (mismatching a type falls through cleanly; raw `'...'` matches literals without placeholders; repeated `{tag}` / `{n as number}:{n}` enforces structural equality; adjacent variable-length placeholders require a delimiter or `: N`). Statement form `match <text> ... end` has optional `else` (`-> <expr>` returns early in `to`, `-> end` exits `loop`, top-level `-> <value>` is disallowed). Expression form requires `else` on `text`, while on a `text` `list` (`it`, `it.index`) it yields a homogeneous result list and `else` is optional (sieve semantics; also accepted as an implicit-return statement inside `to`).
- **Scoping & unified `loop` (`it`, `it.index`, `xs.(expr)`)**: Top-level variables and `def` constants are readable inside `to` functions, but **globals are read-only inside functions** ("Assigned-in-Function = Local": assignments create/update locals without mutating globals; reading a global before a local assignment of the same name fails with `Cannot modify global '...' inside a function...`). Function parameters are immutable. `check` (`->` and `else`) and `loop` are block-scoped. `loop ... end` is a statement, not an expression (`x = loop ...` is invalid; build lists imperatively with `xs = append xs val` inside `loop ... end`, or transform declaratively via `where` / batch `with`). There is only `loop [<list|range>] ... end` (no `for`, `repeat`, `in`, or named loop vars): `loop ... end` without an iterable loops indefinitely (requiring at least one `check <cond> -> end` or early return) and binds `it.index`, while `loop <list|range> ... end` binds both `it` and `it.index` (`def` fields cannot be named `index`). Computed list indexing uses `xs.(expr)` (e.g. `seq.(it.index - 1)`).
- **Data-parallel `swarm loop <iterable> ... end`**: Runs a bounded worker pool over a `list` or `range start end` (`swarm loop` without an iterable is invalid), returning a deterministic `0..N-1` ordered homogeneous `list` (or discarding it in statement position). Outer variables are strictly read-only (`isWorkerRoot`), shared lists are frozen before launch, `say` output is buffered and flushed in `0..N-1` order, `ask` and direct `-> end` are forbidden, `check <cond> -> <expr>` exits only the current worker iteration, and errors report the smallest failing `it.index`. Wrap `(swarm loop ... end)` in parentheses when passing as a function argument or chaining `where`.
- **Background workers & typed inboxes (`spawn`, `inbox as <type>`, `put`, `take`, `close`)**: No `async`/`await` or shared mutable state. Create a buffered (64) typed channel with `ch = inbox as <type>` (`text`, `number`, `def` record, or union; no `bool`/`csv`/`bytes`). Launch any `to` or `mod:fn` call concurrently with `spawn fn arg1 arg2` (args/outer state frozen; globals read-only). Send frozen values with `put ch val` (raises `RuntimeError` if closed), close idempotently with `close ch`, and consume FIFO via `take ch ... end` (`it` and `it.index`, exits automatically when closed & drained, or early via `check <cond> -> end`). Root waits for workers on exit and aborts blocked inboxes on worker failure or `ev.Close()`.
- **Arity-based prefix calls (`def` / `to`)**: `def` = noun blueprint (`def ErrorMessage`), `to` = English infinitive action verb (`to process_response res` — avoid nouns/questions like `to user_data` or `to can_ship`). Call functions directly by name (`process_response res`, `sum_squares range 1 5`, `add (1 + 2) 3`). Every `to`/built-in function has a fixed arity collected in a two-pass parser; function/built-in names cannot collide with variable, constant, or parameter names.
- **No commas in function signatures or calls**: Declare `to add a b ... end` and call `add 2 3`. Commas are only for `list 10, 25, 40` and single-line `with` updates.
- **No `==`, `!=`, `is-not` (asymmetric `is` & union typo protection)**: `<value> is <type>` checks type/union membership (`a is user`, `"OK" is status`, `x is number`), `<value> is <value>` checks structural value equality (`x is 5`, `a is b`). **Types are forbidden on the left side of `is`**: `user is a` or `user is user` raises `TypeError`. Comparing a union-typed value against an invalid string literal (e.g., `d.answer is "yse"` for `"yes" | "no"`) raises `TypeError` (`"yse" is not a value of decision.answer ("yes" | "no")`). Nested `def` record defaults (e.g. `a = pt`) are instantiated as concrete values immediately.
- **Atomic negative literals**: `-2` (no space) is a negative number literal (`f -2`). `a - 2` (space after `-`) is subtraction (`count - 2`). Compound arguments use parentheses (`fib (n - 1)`).
- **Built-in runtime types**: `number`, `text`, `list`, `nothing` (plus `def` records and unions).
- **Raw text vs interpolated text & strict `+`**: `'...'` reads 1:1 with zero `{...}` interpolation and zero backslash escapes (ideal for JSON literals). `"..."` supports `{expr}` interpolation strictly for atomic `text`/`number` values (interpolating a `def` record or `list` raises `TypeError`). `+` never coerces mixed types: only `number + number`, `text + text` (NFC-normalized), and numeric-list addition are allowed (`"41" + 1` or `"x: " + rec` raises `TypeError` — use `"{a}{b}"` or `as text`).
- **Orthogonal Union Types (`def U = A | B | ...`)**:
  - **4 building blocks**: literals (`"OK"`, `404`), base types (`text`, `number`), record blueprints (`ErrorMessage`), and other named unions (automatically flattened: `def outcome = status | ErrorMessage`). Unions can also be used as record field types (`res = outcome`) and typed lists (`list as outcome`).
  - **3 compile-time guardrails**: (1) No redundant literals with `text`/`number` (`'OK' is already covered by 'text'`), (2) No duplicates (`"OK" | "OK"`, `User | User`, or across flattening), (3) Records in the same union (`Admin | Guest`) must differ in at least one mandatory field name, field type, or disjoint inline union constraint so `raw_map as <union>` stays unambiguous.
  - **Type Narrowing & Exhaustiveness in `check`**: Inside `res is ErrorMessage -> ...` (and after an early exit `check res is not ErrorMessage -> ...`), `res` narrows to `ErrorMessage` and allows `res.code` / `res.message`; accessing record fields before narrowing raises a static `TypeError`. A `check ... end` dispatch on a closed union must cover every variant or specify an explicit fallback (`else -> ...` or a post-`end` expression); otherwise compile fails with `Non-exhaustive check on '<union>' (Missing case: ...)`.
- **Explicit JSON + strict `as` contracts (no implicit JSON magic)**:
  - `decode_json raw` parses JSON text -> `map`/`list`/primitives (JSON `true`/`false` become `"true"` / `"false"` text; fails immediately on empty or invalid JSON). `encode_json val` serializes structured data -> JSON text (`def` record fields with `"true" | "false"` union schema serialize back as unquoted JSON booleans `true`/`false`; regular `text` fields and free maps stay JSON strings).
  - `as text` works only on atomic values (`text`, `number`) — records/lists raise `TypeError`.
  - `<map_or_record> as <def_record_or_union>` validates structured data (raw `text` directly -> `TypeError`). **All `def` fields are mandatory** (`Missing field '<type>.<field>'`); extra keys are tolerated.
  - Defaults belong exclusively to `<def> with ...` (`hero = user with id = 1`).
  - **Safe conversion fallbacks (`<expr> as <type> or <fallback>`)**: Allowed for `number`, `text` (scalars/lists), and scalar unions (including string-to-numeric-union conversion like `"404" as HttpCode or 200`). Bare `raw as number` stays a hard `RuntimeError`, while `or <fallback>` binds tighter than arithmetic/comparisons (`raw as number or 0 > 5`), evaluates `<fallback>` lazily (memoized once per batch list like `lines as number or 0`), and enforces strict AOT type matching (`<fallback>` must statically belong to `<type>`/union; plain unannotated `text` vars fail closed unions). Forbidden with `def` records, record-only unions, `bool`, `csv`, `bytes`, and `load ... as ...`.

## 2. Syntax Cheat Sheet
```ease
import network

def pi = 3.14
def status = "OK" | "FAILED"

def ErrorMessage
    code    = 500
    message = "Unknown error"
end

def outcome = status | ErrorMessage

def user
    id   = 0
    name = "Guest"
    role = "guest" | "admin"
end

to process_response res
    check
        res is "OK"         -> "Processed successfully"
        res is "FAILED"     -> "Unknown failure"
        res is ErrorMessage -> "Error {res.code}: {res.message}"
    end
end

to log_only_success res
    check
        res is "OK" -> "Succeeded"
        else        -> "Something else happened"
    end
end

to greet u
    check
        u is not user        -> "Invalid user"
        u.role is "admin"    -> "Admin: {u.name}"
    end
    "Hello {u.name}"
end

to add a b
    a + b
end

# Records, unions, lists, loops, explicit JSON decode + strict contract validation
ada = user with id = 1, name = "Aria", role = "admin"
nums = list 10, 20, 30
first = nums.0
idx = 1
second = nums.(idx)
empty = list as number

loop range 1 3
    check it > 2 -> end
    say "{it.index}: {add it 10}"
end

# `loop xs ... end` binds only `it` and `it.index` (always access record fields via `it.<field>`)
users = list as user with
    id = 1, name = "Aria"
end
loop users
    say "#{it.index} {it.id}: {it.name}"
end

raw_map = decode_json '{"id": 7, "name": "Guest", "role": "admin"}'
parsed = raw_map as user
encoded = encode_json parsed

raw_err = decode_json '{"code": 503, "message": "Unavailable"}' as outcome

parsed_port = match "PORT=8080"
    "PORT={port as number}" -> port
    else -> 0
end

test "example"
    add 2 3 is 5
    parsed_port is 8080
    ("abc" as number or 0) is 0
    ("WARN" as status or "OK") is "OK"
    (swarm loop range 1 3
        it * 10
    end) is list 10, 20, 30
    box = inbox as number
    put box 7
    close box
    take box
        it is 7
    end
    greet ada is "Admin: Aria"
    process_response "OK" is "Processed successfully"
    process_response raw_err is "Error 503: Unavailable"
    log_only_success "OK" is "Succeeded"
    log_only_success raw_err is "Something else happened"
    "abc" as number is error
    '{"id": 7, "name": "Guest", "role": "admin"}' as user is error
    (decode_json '{"id": 7, "role": "admin"}') as user ->
        error.type is "TypeError"
        error.message is "Missing field 'user.name'"
    end
    (ada with id = "bad") is error
    (user is ada) is error
end
```

## 3. Built-in Verbs & CLI
- **Data-driven `test` blocks**: `test "label" ... end` supports assignments, `loop` over test cases, direct boolean conditions (`a + b <= 20`), `is` / `is not`, `expr is error` / `expr is not error`, and `expr -> error.type is "..." / error.message is "..." end` blocks. All assertions run as soft asserts with full enclosing block context on failure (`ease test <file> [--verbose]`).
- **Lists, vector arithmetic, `where` filters, batch `with` & aggregations**: Numeric lists support element-wise `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` (matching lengths required; division/modulo by zero aborts) and scalar broadcasting (`prices * 1.19 + shipping`, `100 - discounts`). Filter lists declaratively with `<list> where <cond>` (single-line `orders where it.status is "paid" and it.amount > 50` or multi-line `where ... end` block with AND-combined conditions and union narrowing on `it`); update record lists uniformly via `cloud with x = it.x + it.vx` (both `where` and batch `with` bind `it` and `it.index`, never implicit fields). Use `append xs item_or_list` to append elements or combine lists (`+` on non-numeric lists raises `TypeError`). Use `sum xs`, `avg xs`, and `sort xs` (returns sorted copy of `number`/`text` lists) for data processing.
- **File I/O (`load` / `save`, no import)**: `load path` / `load path as text` validates UTF-8, strips BOM, normalizes NFC (50 MB max). `load path as bytes` reads raw `0..255` `number` list. `load path as csv` parses uniform CSV into `list` of `map` with original column order (`it.0`, `it.("Header")`, or `it as <def>` with numeric CSV parsing). `save path text_or_bytes` writes UTF-8 text or `0..255` byte list and returns byte count. `csv`/`bytes` are valid only with `load`.
- **Verbs**: `say expr`, `ask prompt`, `count xs`, `type val`, `range start end`, `append xs item_or_list`, `sum xs`, `avg xs`, `sort xs`, `slice xs start end`, `split txt sep`, `join items sep`, `trim txt`, `upper txt`, `lower txt`, `replace txt old new`, `contains txt sub` (condition), `load path [as text|csv|bytes]`, `save path data`, `put box val`, `close box`, `abs n`, `floor n`, `round n`, `min a b`, `max a b`, `fields rec`, `decode_json txt`, `encode_json val`, `fail msg`
- **Semantics notes**: `/` is real floating-point division (`7 / 2` is `3.5`); `range a b` is inclusive (`range 5 1` is empty); recursion is capped at `maxCallDepth = 256` (use `loop` over `range` for deep iterations).
- **File modules**: `import "./file.ease" as mod` (relative `.ease` paths only; cyclic imports raise `ImportError`). Call module functions with `:` (`mod:verb arg1 arg2`), access module `def` records, unions, and constants with `.` (`mod.invoice with ...`, `raw as mod.invoice`, `x is mod.invoice`, `mod.const`). Modules are isolated; module `test` blocks are skipped on import.
- **Standard library (`import network`, `import screen`, `import random`)**:
  - `network` provides HTTP client helpers (`network.network`, `network:fetch target path`, `network:send target path payload`), `inbox`-driven HTTP/TCP servers (`network.http_request`, `network.tcp_client`, `network:serve_http port requests`, `network:reply_text req status body`, `network:reply_json req status data`, `network:serve_tcp port clients`, `network:tcp_send client msg`). Closing `requests` / `clients` closes the listener; closing `client.lines` closes the TCP connection. In `--check` mode, `serve_http` / `serve_tcp` return `0`.
  - `screen` provides `screen.fps_mode` (`number | "unlimited"`, default 60 TPS; `"unlimited"` disables VSync and unlocks TPS), `screen.screen` (`width`, `height`, `title`, `fps`), `screen.event_kind` (`"close" | "key" | "click" | "move"`), `screen.event` (`kind`, `key`, `x`, `y`), `screen:open win events` (binds an `inbox as screen.event` so closing the window emits `"close"` + closes `events`, while `close events` closes the window on next tick), and `screen:present win current_scene` (returns JSON-encoded `screen.frame_state`). Shapes: `circle` and `box` (with `filled = "yes" | "no"`, `stroke = 2`), `line` (`x1, y1, x2, y2, width, color`), `triangle` (`x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, color, filled, stroke`), `label` (`x, y, content, size, color`), unified via `def shape = circle | box | line | triangle | label` (`scene.lines`, `scene.triangles`, `scene.labels`, `scene.shapes`, hex `#RGB`/`#RRGGBB`/`#RRGGBBAA` or named colors). In headless `--check`/`test` mode, `screen:open` emits `key`, `click`, then `close` and closes `events` after 3 frames.
  - `random` provides goroutine-safe randomness via `math/rand/v2` (`random:roll low high` inclusive integer, `random:pick items` element from non-empty `list`, `random:shuffle items` immutable shuffled copy preserving element types).
- **File module alias rule**: `import "./file.ease" as mod` (relative `.ease` paths; call `mod:verb`, access `mod.def` / `mod.const`).
- **CLI**: `ease run <file> [--json] [--check] [--trace]`, `ease serve <file> [--port <n>] [--watch] [--debug] [--debug-port <n>] [--json]` (persistent service runtime with fail-fast startup, worker crash isolation, `--watch` hot-code swapping keeping active `inbox` queues intact, and opt-in `127.0.0.1` debug socket supporting `:status`, `:funcs`, `:reload`, and live Ease evaluation), `ease check <file> [--json]`, `ease test <file> [--json] [--verbose] [--trace]`, `ease build <file> [-o out]`, `ease ast <file> [--json]`, `ease tokens <file>`, `ease lsp`
